previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of chronic abdominal pain was admitted due to worsening epigastric and left lower quadrant pain and acute kidney injury. She had poor oral intake for two days, leading to prerenal azotemia with creatinine rising from a baseline of 1.0 to 1.5, peaking at 1.8, then improving to 1.1 with IV fluids and albumin. Imaging showed cirrhosis without ascites and no evidence of ileus. Urinalysis showed pyuria, but culture revealed fecal contamination, ruling out infection. Pain was attributed to chronic abdominal issues possibly exacerbated by constipation and motility dysfunction. She remained stable without evidence of GI bleeding or hepatic decompensation. She was discharged home with improved renal function, pain control on oral medications, and recommendations to follow up with gastroenterology for motility evaluation and to complete outpatient lab testing.

Mr. ___ is a ___ y/o female with PMH notable for EtOH

___: Cr elevated from baseline 1.0-1.1 to 1.5 on admission. 
Thought likely prerenal in setting of decreased PO intake. It 
resolved uneventfully with IV fluids.

#Abdominal Pain: Patient has extensive hx. of abdominal pain 
with extensive negative work-up including normal EGD, H.Pylori 
negative, celiac negative. Thought to be combination of 
constipation-predominant IBS, cirrhosis, portal hypertension, 
and possibly T10 paraspinal mass. On admission pain appeared at 
baseline. She continued on home regimen of lubiprostone, 
tylenol, simethicone, lidocaine patch, zofran PRN, and tramadol. 
She is recommended to follow up with Dr. ___ for 
possible contribution of motility disorder given her abdominal 
distention and chronic constipation.

#Pyuria: Patient with pyuria on admission, endorsed increased 
urinary frequency. Culture not sent. She was treated with 2 days 
ceftriaxone.

#Melena: Pt has had multiple admissions for reported melena, 
including this admission. H/H remained stable and stools brown 
this admission. Suspect there may be anxiety component that 
causes her to worry about BMs that are not true melena. Given 
recent extensive negative work-up including EGD, colonoscopy, 
and capsule study. EGD x2 from ___ revealed 2 cords of grade 
1 varices in the distal esophagus no further workup was done. 
She was continud on home pantoprazole 40mg IV BID.

#Alcoholic Cirrhosis: Complicated by hepatic encephalopathy, 
grade 1 esophageal varices as above, medically controlled 
ascites per chart review (though pt denies this, is off 
diuretics and without ascites at this time). She was continued 
on lactulose and rifaximin. She had no ascites. Diuretics had 
been held on prior admission and were not restarted in house.

#Psych: Continued citalopram and risperidone
